english.title: Recklessly / negligently permitted an aircraft to endanger person / property
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) on **(..SPECIFY FLIGHT NUMBER AND DEPARTURE AND DESTINATION AIRPORTS WHERE APPROPRIATE..), recklessly or negligently permitted an aircraft, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF AIRCRAFT..), to endanger a person or property by **(..SPECIFY THE ALLEGED ACT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to Articles 138, 241(7) of, and Part C of Schedule 13 to the Air Navigation Order 2009 made under sections 60 and 61 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982.

english.notes:
(i) See Articles 247 and 248 respectively of this Order for details of the extra-territorial effect of the Order when the aircraft is UK registered or when it is foreign registered but over UK territorial waters.
(ii) See the Civil Aviation (Amendment) Act 1996, which amends Section 92 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982, for when the aircraft on which the offence is committed is foreign registered and over foreign territorial waters.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
